title: 07 · Health fact one: Sleep is the maintenance shift

Mira.voice: A mature adult woman with a clear lower mid range English voice, measured documentary delivery, articulate and gently wry.

Rowan.voice: An adult voice with a light medium pitch, clear English, thoughtful conversational delivery and a wry playful tone.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: I slept four hours. But I feel ready to make eight hours of questionable decisions.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Sleep supports attention, memory and emotional well-being. It is maintenance time, not wasted time.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: My brain's night staff keep arriving while I am watching one last video. They have formed a union.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Children aged six to twelve generally need nine to twelve hours. Teenagers need eight to ten. Adults aged eighteen to sixty generally need at least seven.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: So a child is not an adult with a smaller charging cable.

lines.speaker: Mira
lines.text: Protect enough sleep time and keep bedtime and waking time consistent. Regular trouble sleeping deserves attention from a healthcare professional.

lines.speaker: Rowan
lines.text: Tonight, one last video will have an actual definition of last.

direction: Two standing characters converse. Use facial expressions, arm gestures and camera changes. No walking, object handling, physical demonstrations or animated cutaways are required. Let the dry punchlines breathe.

visual.title: Sleep needs change with age
visual.caption: Daily recommendations; individual needs and older-adult guidance vary
